questions.question: Which of the following is not a prime number?
questions.solution:
Checking each number one by one :

⇒ 87 → the sum of digits is 15 which is divisible by 3 clearly → 87 is not a prime number.

⇒ 61 → 61 is only divisible by 1 and 61 → 61 is a prime number.

⇒ 79 → 79 is only divisible by 1 and 79 → 79 is a prime number.

⇒ 89 → 89 is only divisible by 1 and 89 → 89 is a prime number.

∴ 87 is not a prime number.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are true?

I. (√9 - √6) > (√6 - √3)

II. (√6 - √9) > (√3 - √5)
questions.solution:
Clearly, √9 = 3 : √6 = 2.45 : √5 = 2.23 : √3 = 1.73

⇒ √9 - √6 = 3 - 2.45 = 0.55

⇒ √6 - √3 = 2.45 - 1.73 = 0.72

⇒ Clearly, Statement I is wrong.

⇒ √6 - √9 = 2.45 - 3 = - 0.55

⇒ √3 - √5 = 1.73 - 2.23 = - 0.5

⇒ Clearly, statement II is wrong.

∴ Neither I nor II is correct.

How many numbers are there from 11 to 131 which are divisible by both 5 and 7?
questions.solution:
If a number is divisible by both 5 and 7 then the number is divisible by 35.

∴ The first number to be divisible by 35 is 35 and last is 105.

⇒ Let a = 35, d = 35 and An = 105

⇒ 105 = 35 + (n - 1)35 ∵ n is the no. of numbers divisible by 35.

⇒ 105 - 35 = 35n - 35

⇒ n = 105 / 35 = 3

∴ there are 3 numbers divisible by both 5 and 7 between 11 and 131.

questions.question: P alone can do a work in 60 days. P is 40% less efficient than Q. In how many days can Q alone do the same work?
questions.solution:
Let Q can do x amount of work in one day

⇒ P’s work in 1 day = x - 0.4x = 0.6x

But we know P’s one day’s work = 1/60

⇒ 0.6x = 1/60

⇒ x = 1/(60 × 0.6) = 1/36

Q does 1/36 of work in 1 day

∴ Q will finish 1 unit of work in 36 days.

questions.question: Two pipes A and B can alone fill a tank in 6 hours and 9 hours respectively. Pipe C can alone empty the same tank in 6 hours. If all three pipes are opened together, then in how many hours will the tank be filled?
questions.solution:
Tank filled by A in 1 hour = 1/6

Tank filled by B in 1 hour = 1/9

Tank emptied by C in 1 hour = 1/6

Tank filled in 1 hour when all 3 are opened = (1/6) + (1/9) - (1/6) = 1/9

∴ Tank will be filled in 9 hours.

questions.question: A profit of 20% is made after giving a discount of 10% on an article. If the marked price of the article is Rs 2240, then what is its cost price (in Rs)?
questions.solution:
**Short trick∶**

Cost price = 2240 × 0.9/1.2 = Rs. 1680

**Detailed solution∶**

MP = Marked Price

SP = Selling Price

Given : MP = 2240

⇒ SP = MP - 0.1MP = 0.9MP = 0.9 × 2240 = 2016

Profit = 20%

⇒ SP = CP + 0.2CP = 1.2CP

⇒ 1.2CP = 2016

⇒ CP = 2016 / 1.2 = 1680

∴ Cost Price = Rs 1680

questions.question: An article has marked price of Rs 7500 and is available at a discount of 20%. The shopkeeper gives another discount to the buyer and sells the article for Rs 5100. What is the second discount (in %) offered?
questions.solution:
Marked Price = 7500

Initial SP after 20% discount = 7500 - 0.2 × 7500 = 6000

Final SP = 5100

Let x be final discount

⇒ Final SP = 6000 - (x / 100) × 6000 = 6000 - 60x

⇒ 5100 = 6000 - 60x

⇒ 60x = 6000 - 5100 = 900

⇒ x = 900 / 60 = 15

∴ Second Discount = 15%

questions.question: The ratio of two positive numbers is 4 : 7. Their product is 4732. What is the smallest number?
questions.solution:
Let 4x and 7x be the numbers.

⇒ 4x × 7x = 4732

⇒ 28x² = 4732

⇒ x² = 4732/28 = 169

⇒ x = 13

∴ Smallest number = 13 × 4 = 52

questions.question: If the sum of two numbers is equal to six times of their difference, then what is the ratio of the given numbers?
questions.solution:
Let the two number be ‘x’ and ‘y’.

⇒ x + y = 6 × (x - y) = 6x - 6y

⇒ 6y + y = 6x - x

⇒ 7y = 5x

⇒ y = 5x/7

∴ Ratio of x and y = x ∶ y = x ∶ (5x/7) = 7 ∶ 5

questions.question: The average age of a class is 21 years. If a student with age 42 years joins the class, then new average age becomes 24 years. How many total students are there in the class now?

A new student joins with age 42

⇒ Sum of ages of n + 1 students = 24(n + 1) = 24n + 24

⇒ Sum of ages of n + 1 students = Sum of ages of n students + 42

⇒ 24n + 24 = 21n + 42

⇒ 3n = 18

⇒ n = 18 / 3 = 6

But a 42 year student joins become 

∴ Total Students 6 + 1 = 7

questions.question: A sold a car to B at a profit of 20%. B sold the car to C at a loss of 10%. If C pays Rs 432 for car, then for how much (in Rs) A bought the car?
questions.solution:
**Short Trick:**

Cost price for A = 432/(1.2 × 0.9) = Rs. 400

**Detailed Solution:**

Let the cost price for A be x

⇒ Selling price for A = Cost price for B = x + 0.2x = 1.2x

⇒ Selling price for B = Cost price for C = 1.2x - 0.1 × 1.2x = 1.08x

⇒ 1.08x = 432

∴ x = CP = 432/1.08 = Rs 400

questions.question: If oranges are bought at the rate of 9 for a rupee, then how many oranges must be sold for a rupee so as to gain 12.5%?
questions.solution:
For 1 rupee 9 oranges are sold

⇒ Price of 1 orange = 1 / 9

SP for 1 orange for 12.5% profit = 1/9 + 0.125 × (1 / 9) = 1.125 / 9

⇒ 1 orange is sold for 1.125/9 rupees

⇒ 9 / 1.125 oranges will be sold for 1 rupee

∴ for a gain of 12.5% 8 oranges should be sold for 1 rupee.

questions.question: A number is decreased first by 30% and then it is again decreased by 30%. What is the percentage change in the number?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

A number is decreased first by 30%

Then it is again decreased by 30%.

**Concept:**

X% of Y = XY/100

**Calculation:**

Let the number be ‘x’

Number after 1st decrease = x - 0.3x = 0.7x

Number after 2ⁿd decrease = 0.7x - 0.3 × 0.7x = 0.49x

∴ Percentage change = [(x - 0.49x)/x]&am

questions.question: Two numbers are 10% and 20% less than the third number respectively. First number is what percent of the second number?
questions.solution:
Let the third number be x

⇒ First number = x - 0.1x = 0.9x

⇒ Second number = x - 0.2x = 0.8x

Let ‘y’ be the required %

Required % = 0.8x × (y/100) = 0.9x

⇒ y = (0.9/0.8) × 100 = 112.5%

∴ First number is 112.5% of second number.

questions.question: A car travels at a speed of 50 m/s. for 5 hours. What is the distance (in km.) travelled by the car?
questions.solution:
Speed = 50m/s = (50 × 18)/5 = 180 km/hr

Time = 5 hours

∴ Distance = Speed × Time = 180 × 5 = 900 km

questions.question: A 700-metre-long train crosses an 800-metre-long bridge in 27 seconds. What is speed (in km/hr) of the train?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Train length = 700 meter

Bridge length = 800 meter

Time is taken by train to cross the bridge = 27 seconds

**Formula used:**

Speed = Distance/Time

To convert speed from m/s to km/h multiply by 18/5

**Calculation:**

Distance travelled

⇒ 700 m + 800 m = 1500 m

Speed of the train is

⇒ 1500/27 = 500/9 m/s

Speed in km/h

⇒ (500/9) × (18/5) = 200 km/h

**∴ The speed of the train is 200 km/h.**
